My dear [Miss Smith](/person/263),
Thank you for your kind, warm hearted letter. I know you too know what a great grief is, and how close one clings to the last surviving parent,[^2] and the sense of being still a child at home.

May you long preserve that blessing.
I should be very lonely but that my [brother](/person/1624) and his [wife](/person/1604) are only a garden’s length from me, and most kind, and just at present I have a [cousin](/person/1582) with me, who has always been like a sister to me. I think I shall go into Devonshire with her, and then return to face the solitude

yours sincerely

C M Yonge


[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: CMY is replying to a letter of condolence on the death of [FMY](/person/1606), who died on 28 September 1868.

Ann Carter Smith’s father, the Rev.

Richard Carter Smith, perpetual curate of St.

Paul’s Charlton, had died on on 1 October 1864.
